To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) conditioned media (CM) from the human breast cancer cell line MDA-MB 231 (231-CM), increases the secretion of cathepsinB (CTSB) by the human monocyte cell line U937 and 2) the increase in CTSB is mediated by interleukin- 6 (IL- 6) secreted by U937 cells in response to 231-CM.

1) media conditioned by breast cancer cells increase expression and secretion of cathepsin by monocytes; 2) the increases in cathepsin secretion are dependent on the cytokine, IL-6; and 3) IL-6 is a key regulator of monocyte cathepsin expression.

1) media conditioned by MCF-7 and MDA-MB231 breast cancer cells increased U937: proliferation, CTSB expression and secretion, MMP-2 and MMP-9 secretion, and IL-6 and IGFBP-1 secretion; 2) neutralizing antibodies against human IL-6 reduced U937 CTSB secretion induced by MDA-MD231 conditioned media; and 3) U937 cells expressed IL-6 receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cytokines in monocyte activation and protease expression and secretion in the breast cancer microenvironment.
the role of monocytes and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment of breast cancer and their potential as a target of therapy.
the role of tumor-derived soluble factors in the activation of monocytes and their secretion of molecules that promote tumor growth, invasion, metastasis and angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-6 is involved in the increased monocyte expression of CTSB.
our results suggest a novel role for IL- 6 in the tumor microenvironment in promoting breast cancer progression.
IL-6 is one of the factors that increases expression and secretion of cathepsin-B by breast tumor-associated monocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-6 increases expression and secretion of cathepsin by breast tumor-associated monocytes.

the paracrine interaction of breast cancer cells and tumor-associated monocytes in the breast tumor microenvironment results in an increase of CTSB secretion by monocytes, which in turn promotes the invasion and metastasis of breast cancer cells.

breast tumor-associated monocytes are activated by paracrine signals from breast cancer cells, resulting in increased secretion of proteases, which in turn may facilitate tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cytokine, IL-6, increases expression and secretion of the breast tumor-associated protease, CTSB, by monocytes, and that the increased CTSB secretion by monocytes in response to 231-CM may contribute to breast cancer growth, metastasis and invasion.

breast cancer cells secrete soluble factors that can increase expression and secretion of the protease cathespsin B and the cytokines IL-6 and IGFBP-1 by monocytes, and that these effects can be reduced by neutralization of IL-6.
the cytokine IL-6, secreted by breast tumor cells, induces monocyte secretion of the protease cathepisin B, which can promote tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
